name: Zero Talk 11M
summary: An English text-to-speech model with about 11M parameters. It runs in the browser on the user's own device; nothing typed leaves the device.

parameters.counted: stored weights of model.bin, the one voice included; not counted: the scale factors of the 4-bit and 8-bit coding
parameters.voice: built into the weights; another voice would need a new model

size_note: model.bin is the model. The whole download is model.bin plus engine.wasm and frontend.bin (sizes in files).

audio.output_format: WAV or Ogg Opus (the demo's download is .ogg)

engines: WebGPU, where the browser offers it on a secure page
browser.network: The files are fetched once, when the demo starts; speech is made on the device.

tested: Chromium on an Apple-silicon laptop, both engines
Safari 26 on an iPhone 17 Pro, both engines
Packages, in continuous integration: Linux (x86-64 and ARM), Windows (x86-64) and macOS (Apple silicon); Python 3.9 and 3.13; Node.js 22 and 24

measurements.result: 8.0 s of speech made in about 3.2 s, about 2.5 times faster than real time
measurements.build: an earlier build of this page

limitations: Questions come out flat; exclamations do not come across.
Some S sounds have a slight lisp.
Long sentences can lose their rhythm; sentences that open with a greeting and a comma can sound unnatural.
Very short utterances can sound slightly cut off at the start.
No controls for tempo or pauses.
Accented Latin words are read in plain spelling; other scripts are left out with a warning.
The two browser engines give close but not identical audio.

not_in_this_version: control over delivery style and emphasis
